title: Chinese factory activity expands in September amid AI boom
desc: China's factory activity expanded in September, official and private surveys showed on Wednesday, as easing weather disruptions allowed ‌factories to resume operations and a global AI boom supported the industrial sector.

title: What older adults do on screens may matter more than total screen time
desc: Across 8,996 older adults in four cohorts, television viewing was associated with poorer global cognition, while computer use was associated with better cognitive performance, with the strongest positive associations at low-to-moderate levels of use. Mendelian randomization supported these opposing patterns and linked genetically predicted television viewing time to lower left insula volume, which accounted for an estimated 14.8% of its association with poorer cognitive performance.

title: AI and Proteomics Accelerate VAV1 Molecular Glue Discovery
desc: AI-guided structural modeling and proteomics identified molecular glues that degrade VAV1, a potential target in blood cancers and autoimmune diseases.

title: AI transforms crop breeding as first genomics centre opens in the Philippines
desc: Artificial intelligence is helping identify valuable crop traits faster than ever, as the Philippines opens its first agricultural genomics centre to accelerate the development of more resilient and productive crops.

title: Ex-felda DG charged with deceiving board over Jalan Semarak land transfer
desc: KUALA LUMPUR: A former Felda director-general has been charged in the Sessions Court here with deceiving the board of directors over the transfer of land titles belonging to the agency to Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd.

title: Strange giant planet TOI-1355 b set to vanish from view in 2033
desc: Since their first discovery in 1995, hot Jupiter exoplanets (hot Jupiters, for short) quickly challenged our understanding of exoplanet formation and evolution, including exoplanetary system architecture. This is because, as their name implies, they orbit at extremely close distances to their host stars, ranging from a few days to a few hours. Some of their orbits are even oval-shaped, called eccentric in the scientific community, meaning their orbit is oval-shaped. But could such an orbit cause a hot Jupiter to completely vanish from view, preventing astronomers from studying it?

title: Drones, satellites and AI help scientists watch over Antarctica’s smallest lifeforms
